info.title: Asten API
info.description:
The one transport of Asten, a local-first writing desk. The browser desk, the desktop shell's webview, the Word task pane and the Docs sidebar all speak this API, usually over loopback; nothing here reaches any other server.

Pair once with a six-digit code (`POST /api/v1/auth/pair`) and send the token as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`; a browser served by the API itself may rely on the `asten_session` cookie instead. The change stream takes a one-minute single-use ticket in the query string because an EventSource cannot set headers. Token kinds carry authority: `desk` and owner `session` tokens may manage pairing, tokens and the passphrase; `guest` tokens may read and write the story and revoke only themselves. `ASTEN_AUTH` selects the mode (`pairing`, `owner`, `off`); the `x-asten` extension below lists them.

Every error is JSON of the form `{ "error": { "code": "404", "message": "…" } }`. See `docs/API.md` for the curl walk-through and `docs/SECURITY.md` for the threat model.

get.summary: Subscribe to a project's change stream
get.description: Server-sent events. The event names are `revision`, `diagnostics`, `document`, `canon` and `heartbeat`, each with a `StreamEvent` as JSON data; `lagged` (data `{}`) says the client fell behind and should refetch; a `ping` comment arrives every twenty seconds. The first event is a `heartbeat`. Authenticate as usual with the bearer token or the `asten_session` cookie, or, from an EventSource that cannot set headers, with a ticket from `POST /projects/{project_id}/stream-ticket` passed as `?ticket=`: it lives one minute and is spent on first use, so nothing worth stealing reaches a proxy log.

parameters.name: ticket
parameters.description: A stream ticket, instead of the Authorization header or the cookie

401.description: No valid token, cookie or ticket; a ticket that is spent or expired

post.description: A random ticket bound to this project, valid for sixty seconds and spent on first use, for `GET /projects/{project_id}/stream?ticket=…`. Anchor.description:
A block-relative anchor. Offsets count Unicode scalar values inside the
block's plain text, matching Dynodoc's `RichTextPatch` units. User-facing
code converts to grapheme clusters at the boundary.

quote.description: The anchored text at that revision, kept for re-attachment and display.

context_before.description: Up to ~32 scalars before and after the quote, for fuzzy re-attachment.

stale.description: Set when the anchor could not be mapped or re-attached after an edit.

AnchorRevision.description: Where a span of text was valid: the document revision and the block fingerprint.

seq.description: The document's event sequence number at which the offsets were valid.

fingerprint.description: The block's content fingerprint (lowercase hex SHA-256) at that revision.

scope.description: For `Suppress`: scope. Defaults to this occurrence.

requires_auth.description: Whether requests need a token at all.

Baseline.description: A frozen set of accepted marks; only marks new since it are highlighted.

BlockId.description:
A stable block identity. Dynodoc mints ULIDs; today's Asten documents
carry UUIDv7 in `attrs.id`. The engine only requires that the id is
stable, unique, and never reused, so both schemes fit.

Calendar.description: How ticks map to dates, tagged by `kind`. A fictional calendar carries its months and rules beside the tag.

introduced_at.description: Reading position of the scene that introduces the entity, when marked.

pack.description: Which pack owns the rule. Core rules say "scribe".

field.description: A field name, `$node` for a whole-node disagreement, or `$location`.

oneOf.description: World truth: what is actually so in the story world.
Narration. Projects into `World` unless the narrator is marked unreliable.
What a character claims. Does not project into the world.
What a character believes. Projects into their knowledge state only.

A memory or flashback told from a later vantage. Projects into the world
at the remembered time; time placement comes from the scene.

Context.description:
The epistemic frame a statement lives in (§6.3). Contradictions are only
computed inside one context after inheritance.

host.description: Operating system and processor of the machine running the API.

embedded.description: True when the API is embedded in the desktop or mobile shell.

database_path.description: Where the SQLite file lives. Only desk and owner sessions see it.

logs_path.description:
Where the hosting shell writes its log files, when a shell hosts the
API. Only desk and owner sessions see it.

backups_path.description:
Where the hosting shell keeps its launch-time copies of the database.
Only desk and owner sessions see it.

id.description: Stable across re-analysis: hash of code and evidence identities.

probability.description: Calibrated probability that this is a real problem.

message.description: The explanation chain rendered as text.

prefixItems.description:
Where a mark lands. Block-relative when the statement has an anchor; the
whole document otherwise.

quote.description: What the span says, for display.

cached_blocks.description: Count of blocks whose perception came from the cache.

A beat on the timeline: something that happens, with a kind the engine

A value in a predicate's domain. Strings never reach the analyses: concepts,
